description: Substrate materials for the rf-circuit Substrate part and the full-wave templates. Typical values from the manufacturers' data sheets or the literature named in 'source'; verify them for your lot, thickness and frequency.

materials.name: FR-4 (generic)
materials.note: Generic glass-epoxy textbook value. Real FR-4 laminates range from about 3.8 to 4.8 (tan delta 0.015 to 0.025) depending on glass style, resin content and frequency.
materials.source: Generic value, not a data sheet; use the laminate maker's table for a real board

materials.name: Rogers RO4003C
materials.note: Design Dk; the process (clamped stripline) Dk is 3.38 +/- 0.05.
materials.source: Rogers Corporation, RO4000 Series High Frequency Circuit Materials data sheet

materials.name: Rogers RO4350B
materials.note: Design Dk; the process Dk is 3.48 +/- 0.05.
materials.source: Rogers Corporation, RO4000 Series High Frequency Circuit Materials data sheet

materials.name: Rogers RT/duroid 5880
materials.source: Rogers Corporation, RT/duroid 5870 and 5880 data sheet

materials.name: Rogers RO3003
materials.note: Design Dk; the process Dk is 3.00 +/- 0.04.
materials.source: Rogers Corporation, RO3000 Series Circuit Materials data sheet

materials.name: Rogers RO3010
materials.note: Design Dk; the process Dk is 10.2 +/- 0.30.
materials.source: Rogers Corporation, RO3000 Series Circuit Materials data sheet

materials.name: Taconic TLY-5
materials.source: Taconic (AGC Multi Material), TLY data sheet

materials.name: Isola I-Tera MT40
materials.note: Dk and Df depend on the resin content of the construction; the values are those Isola quotes for a representative construction.
materials.source: Isola Group, I-Tera MT40 data sheet

materials.name: Alumina 99.6 % (thin film)
materials.note: Data sheets quote 9.9 at 1 MHz; microwave designs commonly use 9.8 to 9.9. Loss tangent 0.0001 or below.
materials.source: Typical of 99.6 % thin-film alumina data sheets, for example CoorsTek Superstrate 996

materials.name: Fused silica (quartz)
materials.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2011, Appendix H (fused quartz)

materials.name: GaAs (semi-insulating)
materials.note: er is the static dielectric constant. The loss tangent is an order-of-magnitude estimate for semi-insulating wafers and varies from wafer to wafer; use your foundry's value.
materials.source: er: Ioffe Institute semiconductor database (GaAs, static dielectric constant 12.9); tan delta: estimate, not a data-sheet value

materials.name: Silicon, high resistivity (10 kohm cm)
materials.note: The loss of silicon is conduction loss: tan delta = 1/(2 pi f eps0 er rho), here for rho = 10 kohm cm at 10 GHz. It grows as 1/f (0.015 at 1 GHz), so set tand for your frequency and resistivity.
materials.source: er: Ioffe Institute semiconductor database (Si, 11.7); tan delta computed from the resistivity
